reasoning: This record needed the most correction, and two of its factual claims were wrong. First, the previous pass flagged 'MODEL NAME UNVERIFIED - Grok 4.20 could not be independently confirmed as a real xAI release name, possible transcription error'. It is real: data.x.ai/2026-04-07-grok-4-20-model-card.pdf returns 200 direct and opens 'Grok 4.20 System Card / xAI / April 7, 2026'. Second, the previous pass concluded 'NO PUBLISHED MODEL CARD FOR GROK 4.5 OR GROK 4.6 COULD BE LOCATED - recorded as a genuine absence of the document type'. Both cards exist. They are hosted on media.x.ai, not data.x.ai, and the xAI safety hub links them; the hub 403s to curl but reads cleanly through the Wayback id_ raw flag, and extracting its hrefs gives the PDFs, which then fetch 200 direct. The framework claim was also stale: xAI's current Frontier AI Framework is dated 30 June 2026, not 2025. Having recovered the documents, the substantive answer is still None, and here is the closest call in the packet. The Grok 4.6 model card was published with the 2026-08-12 launch, four weeks after the finding, and it does report biosecurity refusal metrics moving in the right direction - Bio refusal recall 97.9% for Grok 4.5 against 100.0% for Grok 4.6 - together with 'dedicated input and topical filters target biological and chemical weapons-related abuse'. But it fails admissibility on substance, not merely on naming. The finding is that a DEPLOYED model's safeguards DEGRADED over three months of external tracking; the card reports pre-deployment metrics for a different, later model on xAI's own internal Autointent-Bio suite, never mentions Grok 4.20, never acknowledges any decline, names no external evaluator anywhere in 42 pages, and is the ordinary content of any launch card. Under the rule that the response must address THIS finding and be attributable to it, that is not a response. Action Level = None; Attribution = No response located. I flag it explicitly as a re-adjudication candidate: an adjudicator who reads same-domain post-finding safeguard improvement as an unattributed response would code this Partial / No explicit attribution, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
